name: Premotor cortex and supplementary motor area
summary: Brodmann area 6 in front of the primary motor cortex: the lateral premotor cortex on the convexity and the supplementary motor area on the medial surface of the superior frontal gyrus in front of the paracentral lobule. Both plan and sequence movements and feed the primary motor cortex, the premotor cortex guiding externally cued movements (reaching for what you see) and the SMA organizing internally generated and bimanual sequences. SMA lesions and surgery produce the transient SMA syndrome of contralateral akinesia and mutism, and SMA seizures produce the dramatic fencing posture.

anatomy.location: Convexity in front of the precentral gyrus (premotor) and the medial surface of the superior frontal gyrus above the cingulate sulcus, in front of the paracentral lobule (SMA), both supplied by ACA and MCA branches at the anterior watershed.

function: Motor planning, sequencing and initiation; bimanual coordination and postural preparation; contribution to speech initiation on the dominant side.

bestView.label: SMA on the medial superior frontal gyrus in front of the paracentral lobule
premotor cortex in front of the precentral gyrus

imaging.normalAppearance: The SMA occupies the medial superior frontal gyrus between the paracentral lobule and a line dropped from the anterior commissure; it is a classic fMRI landmark for surgical planning. Anterior watershed infarcts involve this region.

pathology.finding: Medial superior frontal lesion with contralateral akinesia and reduced speech that recovers over weeks.
Linear infarct along the superior frontal sulcus between ACA and MCA territories.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: DWI and FLAIR; fMRI before resection

lesionEffects.deficit: Contralateral akinesia and hesitancy with preserved strength (SMA syndrome)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of movement initiation, usually transient

lesionEffects.deficit: Apraxia and difficulty with sequences and bimanual tasks

examination: Observe spontaneous movement and speech initiation
Luria three-step sequence and alternating hand movements
Ask about nocturnal seizures with posturing
pearls: Profound weakness-free immobility after a medial frontal stroke or surgery is the SMA syndrome and usually recovers
Bilateral SMA lesions can produce akinetic mutism
